summary: Nine comment-endorsed discoveries across developer tools, home automation, games, and reading.
telegram_footer: 9 items surfaced | 30/30 past front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Prettier
items.source_story_title: Friendship ended with Deno, now Node is my best friend
items.summary: An opinionated code formatter praised by a user across multiple projects.
items.why_included: Clear first-hand approval distinguishes the formatter from neutral runtime comparisons.
items.evidence: AgentME praises Prettier in their projects, while noting the extra dependency and configuration burden in Node projects.

evidence_sources.author: AgentME
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Prettier in other projects and it's also great in those projects, but it's tiring that it's yet another dependency to remember to add and configure in a new node project.

items.name: Tachometer
items.summary: A statistical web benchmark runner using confidence intervals; its repository is archived.
items.why_included: A concrete benchmark runner anchors a practical endorsement of statistically controlled comparisons.
items.evidence: spankalee credits this benchmarking approach with reliable, actionable results and points to Tachometer as the runner implementing it.

evidence_sources.author: spankalee
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is the only way I've been able to get reliable, actionable benchmarks outside of a very, very controlled hardware lab. It's what Google's Tachometer benchmark runner does, and I wish more runners did this:

items.name: LibRaw
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Photoc – Command-line tools for photographers
items.summary: A library for extracting camera RAW data and metadata, recommended by a happy user.
items.why_included: An unaffiliated user explicitly recommends a concrete component for photographic tooling.
items.evidence: tonyarkles recommends LibRaw and identifies themselves as a happy user with no affiliation.

evidence_sources.author: tonyarkles
evidence_sources.excerpt: Check out https://www.libraw.org/! No affiliation, just a happy user.

items.name: GEOPHIRES
items.summary: An open-source geothermal techno-economic simulator; the linked v2 repository is archived.
items.why_included: A direct recommendation turns a broad energy discussion into an actionable modeling resource.
items.evidence: hnmullany recommends the open-source GEOPHIRES model as a starting point for geothermal mathematics and notes its UI.

evidence_sources.author: hnmullany
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you want the ACTUAL mathematics of geothermal energy - a good place to start is the open source GEOPHIRES model which is available on github and has a UI

items.name: Battery Notes
items.source_story_title: Best-selling Zigbee temperature sensors tested and compared
items.summary: A Home Assistant integration tracking battery replacements for clearer sensor-life measurements.
items.why_included: Positive first-hand use gives this small maintenance tool a practical, specific benefit.
items.evidence: moogly uses Battery Notes replacement timestamps to get a clearer view of sensor battery life.

evidence_sources.author: moogly
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Battery Notes in HA which keeps a timestamp since you last changed the battery so I have a pretty good view into battery life

items.name: SONOFF SNZB-02P
items.source_story_title: Best-selling Zigbee temperature sensors tested and compared
items.summary: A Zigbee temperature/humidity sensor with a magnetic mount and CR2477 battery.
items.why_included: A user's replacement choice and approval of the magnetic mount provide concrete endorsement.
items.evidence: moogly replaced most of their previous sensors with SNZB-02P units and likes the built-in magnet despite the thicker body; their three-to-four-year battery estimate is an expectation, not a measured result.

evidence_sources.author: moogly
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've replaced most of them with Sonoff SNZB-02P which runs a CR2477 battery and I expect the battery life to be at least 3 years; with some luck maybe 4? Not as slim however, but the built-in magnet makes up for it.

items.name: Zen Puzzle Garden
items.source_story_title: Samon: Designing a Zen Garden Raking Puzzle
items.summary: A Japanese rock-garden raking puzzle praised for its polished player experience.
items.why_included: A player's clear preference surfaces a concrete alternative to the submitted game.
items.evidence: robinhouston recalls enjoying Zen Puzzle Garden and finds it more enjoyable and polished than Samon.

evidence_sources.author: robinhouston
evidence_sources.excerpt: I find it much more enjoyable to play than Samon. The player experience feels a lot more polished.

items.name: Quarks and Leptons
items.source_story_title: Nobel Prize in Physics 2026: Francis Halzen
items.summary: Halzen and Martin's introductory particle-physics textbook, warmly endorsed by a reader.
items.why_included: An explicit reader endorsement offers a substantive resource beyond the Nobel headline.
items.evidence: cowang says they loved the Halzen and Martin book and links its Internet Archive record.

evidence_sources.author: cowang
evidence_sources.excerpt: Absolute loved this book by Halzen and Martin

items.name: The Deep History of Your Apps
items.summary: A Computer History Museum article tracing NeXTSTEP and early object-oriented programming.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly recommends this historical account alongside the Smalltalk discussion.
items.evidence: slowin recommends the article as a good history while discussing Smalltalk's influence on NeXTSTEP and Objective-C.
